# Sampling With and Without Replacement {#sec-replacement-sampling}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Learning objectives"}
- Differentiate independent draws and finite-list selection.
- Explain why the sampling fraction can affect variance.
:::

## The idea

**With replacement**, a selected unit may be drawn again and successive draws can be modelled as independent under simple random sampling. **Without replacement**, a selected unit is not eligible for later draws. If a substantial fraction of a finite population is sampled without replacement, the usual independent-draw standard error can be larger than the appropriate finite-population standard error.

## When and how to apply it

For a simple random sample without replacement from $N$ units, a familiar finite correction to the standard error is $\sqrt{(N-n)/(N-1)}$. This principle motivates Chapter 11, but requires the relevant finite-population sampling assumptions.

## Formula at a glance

$$
\mathrm{FPC}_{SE}=\sqrt{\frac{N-n}{N-1}}
$$


## Teaching case 1 — baseline draft

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Clinical scenario / initial worked example"}
Place 20 numbered cards in a container. Draw five cards, first returning each card before the next draw, and then repeating without returning cards. Compare possible duplicates and interpretation.
:::

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple" title="Common error"}
Sampling without replacement does not justify FPC for every clinical or experimental design.
:::

## Hands-on exercise

List the number of unique people who might be represented under each method and explain why the sampling procedures differ.

With-replacement and without-replacement sampling are different probability mechanisms.
